clue.text: Wise old bird of Old St. Paul's?

definitions.text: Wise old bird of Old St. Paul's?

parts.note: King Solomon is the byword for wisdom
an eagle is a bird of prey

explanation.surface: A sage old owl perched on the dome of the old cathedral.
explanation.walkthrough: Solomon Eagle is the plague-year fanatic who roams Harrison Ainsworth's novel Old St Paul's; his names are the wise king and a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The character is a figure in Ainsworth's historical novel set around the medieval cathedral of London.

clue.text: Shoots greenhorns

explanation.surface: Firing at novices.
explanation.definitionFit: Suckers are new growths from a plant's root, and also gullible dupes.

clue.text: "Here at the quiet — of the world" (Tennyson)

definitions.text: "Here at the quiet — of the world" (Tennyson)

parts.words: "Here at the quiet — of the world" (Tennyson)
parts.note: a gap-fill from the opening of Tennyson's poem Tithonus

explanation.surface: A line of Victorian verse with a word missing.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word is the edge or boundary, from Tennyson's poem about the aged Tithonus.

clue.text: Swings the lead while Mum hangs about

parts.note: Ma is a word for mother
to linger is to hang about

explanation.surface: A child shirks work while their mother loiters nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: To swing the lead is British slang for shirking by feigning illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Shirking by pretending to be ill is exactly what the idiom describes.

clue.text: He's in line but crookedly

indicators.note: the word line is set crooked, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone standing in a queue that is not straight.
explanation.definitionFit: Neil is a man's name, a typical 'he'.

clue.text: She, being not in favour, has made off

parts.note: anti means against
gone means departed

explanation.surface: A woman who, unpopular, has run away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'She' is a cue for a woman's name; Antigone is the heroine of Sophocles' tragedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Antigone is a woman of Greek myth, daughter of Oedipus.

clue.text: Fall from luxurious circumstances ?

parts.note: dropping out of the lap of luxury; the word for a slip begins with that lap

explanation.surface: Coming down in the world after a life of comfort.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapse is a fall or slip, and the clue plays on the lap of luxury.

clue.text: Pertaining to Byron's prince of poets "

definitions.text: Pertaining to Byron's prince of poets

parts.words: Pertaining to Byron's prince of poets
parts.note: Byron hailed the author of Paradise Lost as the prince of poets

explanation.surface: A question of literary appreciation among the Romantics.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes the style of the author of Paradise Lost, whom Byron praised so.

clue.text: Plaster of Rome ?

parts.note: an Italian word for a fine plaster used on walls and mouldings

explanation.surface: Like plaster of Paris, but from the Italian capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Stucco is fine plaster for coating walls, its name borrowed from Italian.

clue.text: Make a grievance of one's ailment ?

explanation.surface: Someone turning a minor illness into a formal protest.
explanation.definitionFit: A grievance aired is a protest, and an illness is also called by the same word, as in a chest disorder.

clue.text: Compass direction for Jack

explanation.surface: Telling a sailor called Jack which way to head.
explanation.definitionFit: The thirty-two compass bearings are each named that, and a jack is an electrical socket, a power outlet in British usage.

clue.text: Out from under canvas for a stretch

parts.note: the Latin prefix ex- means out of or from
to be under canvas is to be camping in a tent

explanation.surface: Leaving the campsite to go for a long walk.
explanation.definitionFit: Extent is the reach or expanse of something, a stretch of land or time.

clue.text: Cigar set have a rustic air

indicators.note: the cigar and set letters are made to take on a new form, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A box of cigars that smells of the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Agrestic is a learned adjective for things belonging to fields and the country.

clue.text: English county that sends Americans into transports

explanation.surface: A home county whose charms delight visiting Americans.
explanation.walkthrough: Surrey is a county south of London; in America a surrey is a light four-wheeled carriage, so it carries Americans about.
explanation.definitionFit: The county lies just south of London, and the American carriage takes its name from it.

clue.text: Artist tries madly to get in one, butt they're hard to find

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician

indicators.note: the scrambled word takes in the numeral letter

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A painter frantically attempts entry but finds things scarce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'madly' makes RITES from TRIES, and 'to get in' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Rarities are uncommon things, scarce and seldom met.

clue.text: Suggestion of a hostelry that's top-class and there's an end o't

parts.note: an inn is a hostelry
U means upper-class, as in U and non-U
taken as written
o' is the clipped form of 'of', standing as the letter O

explanation.surface: A hint about a smart inn, and that is the final word on the matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'And there's an end o't' is an old Scots phrase meaning that settles it; o't is 'of it'.
explanation.definitionFit: An innuendo is an indirect hint or insinuation.

clue.text: Register with The Times

parts.note: the London paper began life in 1785 as The Daily ... Register

explanation.surface: Signing up with the newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The Times was founded as The Daily Universal Register and renamed in 1788.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word completes the original title of the newspaper.

clue.text: Irishman told to get up but not to take cards

parts.note: to stand is to get up
Pat is a stock Irish name

explanation.surface: An Irishman is ordered to rise.
explanation.walkthrough: In poker, to stand pat is to keep one's hand and draw no new cards.
explanation.definitionFit: In poker one who keeps the hand dealt and declines a draw is said to do this.

clue.text: Just the place for a rubber plantation but in need of a host

parts.note: Pará in Brazil gave its name to Para rubber
a site is a place

explanation.surface: An ideal spot for growing rubber trees that still lacks an owner.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces come in answer order PARA then SITE: a site for Pará rubber.
explanation.definitionFit: A parasite lives on another organism, which is its host.

clue.text: Uncle's so brave !

explanation.surface: Praising an uncle's courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncle' is old slang for a pawnbroker, the one who receives a pledge; a brave is a Native American warrior.
explanation.definitionFit: The receiver of a pawned item is this, and a warrior of the Plains nation is one.

clue.text: Prince makes a strategic movement

indicators.note: the prince's letters make something new, a sign of an anagram

explanation.surface: A royal commander devises a clever manoeuvre.
explanation.definitionFit: A pincer movement is a military manoeuvre enveloping both enemy flanks.

clue.text: A steely response

parts.note: a counter-thrust with a steel blade in fencing

explanation.surface: Answering with cold resolve.
explanation.definitionFit: A riposte is a quick counter-thrust in fencing, and a quick retort.

clue.text: Time for the coven to gather?

definitions.text: Time for the coven to gather?

parts.words: Time for the coven to gather?
parts.note: witches meet at midnight, the hour named after their kind

explanation.surface: Asking when the witches meet.
explanation.definitionFit: The witching hour is midnight, when witches were said to be abroad.

clue.text: Prophet's counterpart to " Thalatta " ?

explanation.surface: A biblical seer mirroring a Greek cry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thalatta!' (the sea!) was the cry of Xenophon's Greeks; an English counterpart would be 'Ho, sea!'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hosea is an Old Testament minor prophet, and split up the name gives a sailor's call on sighting the ocean.

clue.text: Support needed by Jones's neighbours ?

explanation.surface: Neighbours of the Jones family needing help.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom is keeping up with the Joneses, so the neighbours must do this.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold something up is to sustain it, and the idiom of rivalry with the Joneses uses the same phrase.

clue.text: Music-maker in Utopia, no doubt

indicators.note: the instrument sits inside the words Utopia, no

explanation.surface: An instrument found in an ideal world, surely.
explanation.definitionFit: A piano is a keyboard instrument that produces music.

clue.text: Whither Mavourneen was pressed to return

definitions.text: Whither Mavourneen was pressed to return

parts.words: Whither Mavourneen was pressed to return
parts.note: the Irish song 'Come back to ..., Mavourneen' names the place

explanation.surface: Asking where the beloved of a song was urged to come home to.
explanation.definitionFit: Erin is a poetic name for Ireland, named in the old ballad.

clue.text: Quits about seven

indicators.note: turned about, the letters of seven are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone stopping at around seven o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: Being quits means being level, all square, with nothing owed.

clue.text: They're Lutetian in origin

parts.note: Lutetia was the Roman name of the French capital, so its natives are meant

explanation.surface: A remark on a people's ancient ancestry.
explanation.definitionFit: Lutetia was the Roman town that became France's capital, so its citizens descend from it.

clue.text: Starve and lose just about nothing-what a game!

parts.note: to starve is to fast

indicators.note: the word lose sits just about, around, the letter for nothing

parts.note: O looks like zero

explanation.surface: Going hungry and losing almost everything in a reckless game.
explanation.walkthrough: Fast and loose was an old cheating game at fairs, hence 'play fast and loose'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a sharper's trick played with a looped strap at fairs.
